tasks.short: Assign firefighters to locations during a fire.

steps.what: See where rescue of persons is needed now.
Choose strategic locations to maximize application of extinguishing agents.
Assign firefighters to facilitate that rescue.

tasks.design: She sees who needs rescue, chooses the locations, and assigns firefighters by voice. No assignment record is filled, no alert is raised, and nothing is sent outside the crew. No system is configured.
tasks.previous_blocker: The posts depend on what she sees in that minute, and a wrong post can trap a person.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new lets a desk tool see the fire or the people. The assignment stays spoken.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see the rescue need and pick the posts while the fire moves.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can match the people she sees to the firefighters beside her.
tasks.altitude: Her week on the fireground does not change. She still decides the posts.

reach.task: Work the job she assigns at that location.
reach.learn: When to move, and which extinguishing job is theirs.

evidence.claim: Assigning firefighters during a fire is live judgement on the scene. Model knowledge.
Article 22 applies to staff decisions based solely on automated processing.
Works council consent covers working-time and rest-time rules and staff monitoring. Effects of the work on staff are a council matter.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
Firefighters on this crew are colleagues. The spoken assignment is an order to them, not a message outside the organisation, and no version is filed.
No assignment list, alert, or sheet is filled or sent. No roster system and no staff monitor is added, so consent for working time or monitoring is not triggered by this task.
She assigns the people herself, so no solely automated staff decision is made.
unknowns: Whether this company fire crew assigns posts only by voice, or also marks them on a board.
Whether a public fire service is already in command when she assigns her own crew.
research_questions: Does this company assign fireground jobs by voice only?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a fire where she sees the trapped people and assigns the crew by voice, no step is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pass fire details by radio to crew and dispatch.

steps.what: Hear the fire details on the scene.
Decide which of those fire details to pass.
Communicate fire details to superiors and subordinates using radios.
Communicate those details to interagency dispatch centers.

tasks.design: She hears the fire, chooses the details, and speaks them by radio. Superiors and subordinates are inside the organisation. The call to an interagency dispatch center is her own voice, and no transcript, form, or alert is filed or sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The details change as she watches, and the radio call has to be spoken then, not drafted later.
tasks.enabler_now: A transcript of a recording does not speak the next message. She still talks.
tasks.still_hard: She must choose what the crew and dispatch need before the next minute.
tasks.human_edge: The voice on the radio is hers, because a late or wrong detail can harm people.
tasks.altitude: Her week does not change. She still decides what goes on the radio and speaks it.

reach.task: Act on the fire details she gives over the radio.
reach.learn: Which details change the work in front of them.

evidence.claim: Passing fire details by radio is live speech on the scene. Model knowledge.
Article 5 bans emotion recognition at work.
An Anchorage police trial found no real time-savings advantage for drafted narratives, because review ate the time saved.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
Superiors and subordinates are colleagues. The interagency dispatch center is outside the organisation. Both calls are live radio by her. No written version is filed, so there is no commit to gate.
No transcript, alert, or dispatch form is produced. Emotion is not read from the voice.
The Anchorage finding is about drafted police narratives, not this fire. This design does not draft the radio call.
unknowns: Whether every fire is reported to an interagency dispatch center, or only fires the public service attends.
Whether superiors hear the same radio net as the crew.
research_questions: Which fires does this crew report to a dispatch center outside the company?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a fire where she speaks the details by radio to the crew and to dispatch, no step is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead a fire crew while working the fire.

steps.what: Serve as a working member on the engine, hand, helicopter, or prescribed fire.
Be the working leader of that crew of three firefighters.

tasks.design: She works the fire with the crew and leads those firefighters by voice. No crew record, camera, or alert is added, and nothing is sent outside the crew. No system is configured.
tasks.previous_blocker: The crew leader is on the line, not at a desk, and the fire does not wait for a plan.
tasks.enabler_now: No scheduler stands in for her on the line. She still works and leads.
tasks.still_hard: Three or more firefighters still need her voice and her hands on that crew.
tasks.human_edge: She is in the crew, so she sees the line and can change the order at once.
tasks.altitude: Her week does not change. She still works the fire and leads the crew.

reach.task: Work under her on the engine or the prescribed fire.
reach.learn: How this crew leader wants the line run.

evidence.claim: Leading a fire crew while working the fire is physical work on the scene. Model knowledge.
Annex III lists worker management and monitoring as high-risk.
A data protection impact assessment is mandatory for systematic employee monitoring and for body-worn cameras.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
Leading the crew is direction of colleagues. Working the engine, the hand line, the helicopter, or the prescribed fire is her own physical work. Neither act files a version.
No camera, no crew-monitoring record, and no alert is added. No roster is built from this scene.
unknowns: Whether this supervisor's crew is an industrial engine crew, a hand crew, or also runs prescribed fire.
Whether helicopter work is in this company's scope at all.
research_questions: Which crew types does this supervisor actually lead?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a shift where she works the engine and leads the crew in person, no step is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge the size, location, and condition of a fire.

steps.what: Evaluate the size and location of the fires.
Judge the condition of those fires.

tasks.design: She looks at the size and location, then judges the condition herself. No size record is filled or sent, and no camera or alert is added. No system is configured.
tasks.previous_blocker: Size, location, and condition are what she sees, and they change while she looks.
tasks.enabler_now: No model in this design looks at the fire. The judgement stays hers.
tasks.still_hard: A miss on size or condition can harm the crew, so the look stays with her.
tasks.human_edge: She is standing at the fire, so the size and condition are hers to judge.
tasks.altitude: Her week does not change. She still judges the fire by eye.

reach.task: Inspect after the fire she sized.
reach.learn: The size, location, and condition she saw, as spoken, not as a stored score.

evidence.claim: Judging the size, location, and condition of a fire is done by looking at it. Model knowledge.
A data protection impact assessment is mandatory for body-worn cameras.
Article 5 bans emotion recognition at work, and real-time remote biometric identification in public for police has only narrow exceptions.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
Evaluating the fire is looking and judging. No size record is filed or sent, and no camera is added.
No alert is raised by a system. Emotion and identity are not read from the scene.
unknowns: Whether she must write the size and condition after the fire, or only say them.
Whether a second officer must agree the size before she acts on it.
research_questions: Is a written size note part of this role, or only the spoken judgement?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a fire she sizes by eye, no step is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still assigns crews, speaks on the radio, leads the crew, and judges the fire. No desk tool takes those acts.
reach: Firefighters learn the post she assigns and the line she wants run.
A fire inspector learns the size, location, and condition she saw, as spoken rather than as a stored score.
skills_to_grow: Refuse an assignment a model or a map picks for the people on the fire.
Refuse a radio transcript or a dispatch message that files or sends itself.
Refuse a camera or a score of the fire or of the crew.
role.ambitious_version: The same supervisor still assigns, speaks, leads, and judges on the fireground. No record is filed in her place.
